comment: Adopted in 2020 with first use in 2022. Used for all state and federal general elections. All uses except presidential election use the “top four” form, with an open primary advancing 4 candidates to the general election with RCV.
Adopted in 2020, with proportional ranked choice voting first used in November 2022.
Adopted for town council elections since the early 20th century. Uses proportional RCV to elect the city’s seven at-large board of assessors seats.
Adopted in December 2022 for June 2023 primary elections.
Adopted in 2002 for mayoral races with three or more candidates. First used in 2020.
Adopted in 2016 for county commissioner offices (an at-large numbered post) and sheriff. First used in November 2020. Used every November of even years.
Adopted in 2004 and used since 2010 to elect the mayor, city council and city auditor (all single-winner contests). Elections every November of even years.
Adopted in 2020 to elect the mayor district council seats, and at-large council seats. First used in November 2021.
Adopted in 2020 for elections for mayor, starting in November 2023.
Adopted in 2021 for elections for mayor and city council, starting in November 2023.
Adopted by voters in 2021 for city council elections, and expanded in 2023 to cover all other local elections. First used in December 2022.
Adopted in 1941. Uses proportional RCV to elect nine at-large city council seats and six at-large school board seats.
Adopted in 2002 for mayoral races with three or more candidates. Not yet used as of 2022.
Adopted by the city council in 2022. First used in 2022.
Adopted in 2019 for mayoral and all single-seat city council elections. First used in 2021.
Adopted in 2018 and used since 2019 for all municipal elections, including mayor and council by district.

Adopted in 2016 for state and federal primary elections and all general congressional elections. First used in 2018. Expanded to be used for presidential elections beginning in 2020 (presidential general election) and 2024 (presidential primaries).

Adopted in 2006 and used since 2009 in elections for 22 city offices, including mayor and city council in single-winner elections, and some park board and board of taxation seats using proportional RCV.
Adopted in 2020 for mayor and city council. First used in 2021.
Adopted in 2019 for city primary and special elections for mayor, other citywide offices, borough presidents and city council. First used in 2021.
Adopted in 2006 and used since 2010 for a total of 18 city offices, including mayor and city council (all single-winner contests).

Adopted in 2010 for mayor and first used in 2011. Expanded in 2020 to apply to city council and school board seats. In 2022 voters approved a ballot measure authorizing the city council to adopt proportional RCV for multi-winner elections, with first implementation anticipated in November 2023.
Adopted in 2002 and used since 2004 to elect mayor, city attorney, board of supervisors and other citywide offices (all single-winner contests).
Adopted as option in 2000 charter amendment and used since 2010 to elect mayor and city council (elected at-large, by numbered post).
Adopted in 2008 and used since 2018 for mayor, city council and municipal judge (all single-winner contests).
Adopted in 2018 and used since 2019 for mayor and city council races (at-large by numbered post).
Adopted in 2009 and used since 2011 to elect mayor and the city council (all single winner contests).
Adopted in 2006 and used since 2007 in all elections for mayor and city council (all single-winner contests).
